Polar diagram

The light's shape, all layers combined. Solid: seen from the side, Front on the right. Dashed: seen from the front, Right on the right. Straight down is at the bottom; rings are in candela.

Photometry

Beam is where the light falls to half brightness, field to 10%; both read front-to-back × side-to-side. Upward light is the share of output above the horizon.

IES file text

In Unreal, drag the .ies into the Content Browser and assign it to a light's IES Texture. Unpack the .zip first, or rename the .txt to end in .ies. Straight down here is the light's forward direction in Unreal. Recent UE5 versions use Front, Left, Back and Right separately (C0, C90, C180, C270 in the file); older ones use one curve. Use the Orientation test preset to see which way Front faces.

Layers

Layers stack bottom to top and combine into the exported light. The curve editor and the preview handles shape the selected layer.

    Add: like a second bulb. Lighten: the brighter wins. Replace: paints over. Mask: a stencil for the layers below. Subtract: removes light.

    Modifiers

    Curve generator

    Builds a curve from a few settings. The dashed violet line in the editor previews it before you apply.

    Intensity scale

    File settings

    Candela values are written with a multiplier of 1. Use Absolute (−1) if your importer rescales by the lumen figure. With noise, rays, a turn or an imported file the file uses at most 2.5° horizontal steps; pick 1° for the finest detail.

    3D view

    Drag to orbit (also below the floor or above the ceiling, where they drop out), scroll or pinch to zoom, double-click to reset. Uses the floor height, wall distance and side, and the preview look. A ceiling appears for upward light.
